answer: An agent marketplace requires a $100 bond for each $20 job and forfeits it if no valid result arrives by the deadline, using an agreed machine-checkable test. Fake accounts may spread like a vine, but every concurrent job needs its own bond; new names offer no cheap haven. Through this prism, identity matters less than collateral: an attacker running 1,000 fake workers must lock $100,000 and loses those bonds if the workers default.
